findings.issue: Repeated `pkill -f "react-router-serve"` after already diagnosing at trace.md:798 that the pattern matches its own wrapping shell and SIGTERMs it; cost ~4 turns of restart probes (turns 64-67)
findings.suggestion: After the first occurrence, kill by recorded PID (or use a bracket pattern like `react-router-serv[e]`, which it did only at cleanup in turn 71) and never put the pkill and the restart in the same shell command

findings.issue: Ran the Playwright screenshot script from /tmp, so `@playwright/test` could not be resolved (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND)
findings.suggestion: Write scratch scripts that import repo dependencies inside the repo (or use NODE_PATH), as it correctly did on the retry

findings.issue: Turn-41 curl|python probe printed 'MISSING' for content that was actually present (accented characters / fragile regex pipeline), briefly suggesting the Pokémon page was broken
findings.suggestion: Save the response to a file and use simple substring/grep checks (as it did in turn 42) before concluding content is missing

findings.issue: Pinned @types/react@^19.3.1 without checking it existed, failing the first install
findings.suggestion: Run `npm view` before pinning exact versions (it did this for react-router but not for the types packages)

findings.issue: The meta({ data }) title bug's exact root cause was never pinpointed; it pivoted to the React 19 <title> approach per v8 docs
findings.suggestion: The pivot is defensible and idiomatic for v8, but confirming the root cause first (one console.log of meta args) would have cost one turn and removed the ambiguity

summary: A disciplined, well-sequenced session: thorough upfront recon of spec, tests, data, and design led to a complete first-pass implementation whose very first full test run passed 54/54 with zero fix cycles. Debugging was systematic and docs-driven (unused .server import, v8 meta vs React 19 title). The only real waste was repeating a self-inflicted pkill footgun and a few avoidable bash mistakes, costing roughly 8 of 72 turns.
